about: Every command the Developer doctrine and the rendered brief name, one entry each. `forms` are the exact command forms read off the texts (command-sources.ts); `run` is the command the suite runs inside each agent's sandbox, from the task worktree; an entry with `notRun` instead names why no Developer runs it inside its sandbox. `{tranche}` and `{n}` are a tranche task that is dispatchable now, found by the suite; an entry with `needsDispatchableTask` runs only when one exists, and an entry with `needsPrBody` runs only when the branch has an open pull request, with its body as `PR_BODY` — each runs on inputs it can pass on, so a failure is the sandbox's.

forms: git log origin/main..HEAD --format="%s" | awk '{ if (length > 72) print NR": "length" chars (OVER LIMIT): "$0 }'
commands.run: git log origin/main..HEAD --format="%s" | awk '{ if (length > 72) print NR": "length" chars (OVER LIMIT): "$0 }'
gh issue view 1026 --json number,title; echo "gh exit $?"

commands.notRun: re-asserts a brief's Premise block — it needs the dispatched brief text as its body file, which only a real dispatch has
judges the PR body the Developer wrote (PR_BODY); with no body its verdict is about the body, never the sandbox
writes an empty changeset file into the diff for a no-release change — it changes the worktree, and the sandbox is already proven by the entries that read and write it
the composite of typecheck, format-and-lint, the pre-push test selection and verify-docs — the driver runs it at PR-open time, and its sandbox-relevant parts are entries of their own here
the pre-push hook's own command — under the review loop the driver pushes, outside the sandbox, and the doctrine forbids hand-running it
the doctrine forbids a local full-suite run — CI's shards run it
the driver creates the task worktree, outside any sandbox, before the Developer's first turn

under the review loop the Developer publishes through the driver-run dev-tools (publish_changes), outside the sandbox, and holds no git push of its own; the manual-path forms are named for a human at a terminal

under the review loop the Developer opens and updates the pull request through the driver-run dev-tools (open_pull_request/update_pull_request_body/refresh_evidence), outside the sandbox; the manual-path report forms are named for a human at a terminal
the Operator's and the driver's commands — they start a Developer, never run inside one

forms: gh pr list --state merged --json number,headRefName,mergedAt | jq '[.[] | select(.headRefName | startswith("task/<tranche>/"))] | sort_by(.mergedAt) | last'
commands.notRun: the superseded prior-archival precondition — preserved as history, the doctrine says not to enforce it
named, not run: the CLI's name and invocation shape, a status read and a token read for a human, bare git stash (the doctrine forbids it), and an anti-pattern's example
